_query_rationale: MONEY-1238 — this query was rebuilt because the previous one could not fire
for any job in any environment. Three independent faults, all in one line:
1. It queried `job.written`. `packages/datadog/src/metrics.ts` initialises
datadog-metrics with `prefix: METRIC_PREFIX` ('stockbook.'), so the
series that exists is `stockbook.job.written`. The monitor watched a
name nobody emits — permanently NO DATA, and a NO DATA alert that is
always firing is a NO DATA alert that gets muted.
2. It substituted `env:prod`. The workers emit `env:${getDatadogEnv()}`,
and workers/cloudbuild.prod.yaml sets DD_ENV=production, so the tag on
prod is `env:production`. QA matched by coincidence (qa -> qa), which
is why nobody caught it: the environment it was tested in was the one
environment where it worked.
3. `job.selected` appeared in the comment above and in
docs/reference/xbrl-switchover-runbook.md, but in NO query. Without it
the alert is 'written == 0', which fires on every genuinely idle run —
precisely the distinction the two counters exist to draw.
## Why clamp_max and not a composite monitor
The condition is a CONJUNCTION (selected > 0 AND written < 1), which a
single threshold cannot express directly. Datadog's own answer is a
composite monitor — but a composite references its children BY ID, so
provisioning one needs three API calls per job and leaves three monitor
objects to keep in sync, two of which alert on their own. apply-monitors.sh
provisions each job in ONE request, and a script that is one request per job
is a script that can be re-run without reasoning about partial state.
`clamp_max(x, 1)` maps any positive count to 1 and leaves 0 at 0, so the
difference of the two clamped counts is exactly the truth table wanted:
selected  written  clamped diff   alerts?
> 0       0        1 - 0 = 1      YES — found work, produced nothing
> 0       > 0      1 - 1 = 0      no  — healthy
0         0        0 - 0 = 0      no  — genuinely idle
0         > 0      0 - 1 = -1     no  — wrote without selecting (backfill)
The threshold is therefore `> 0` with `thresholds.critical = 0`, and it is
count-scale-free: no per-job tuning, nothing to drift.
`.as_count()` on both sides because these are COUNTERS: `sum(last_36h)` of a
counter without it is a rate average, which can round a single small run to
a value that clamps wrong.
name: [{{env}}] {{job}} wrote nothing but had work to do
message:
{{job}} selected rows and wrote none in the last {{window}}.

This is the 'runs, succeeds, writes nothing' class (MONEY-1220). The schedule is healthy and the invocation returned 200 — check the job's structured `job-outcome` line for `skippedReason`, which names which door closed.

Usual causes, in order of how often they have actually happened here:
  1. A Cloud Run JOB pinned to a stale image (deploying the SERVICE does not move it)
  2. A population/tier gate matching zero rows
  3. An env var unset, so a provider never registered
  4. An upstream returning 403/404 to our egress while the job swallows it

@{{notify}}
_notify_no_data_rationale: notify_no_data is TRUE on purpose. A job emitting no metric at all is not a
quiet success — it is a job that did not run, or one whose reporting call
was removed. Both are exactly what this monitor exists to catch, and both
look identical to 'everything is fine' without it.
MONEY-1238 — this option is also the reason the monitor list and the emit
sites have to be kept in step by a test rather than by intention. Four of
the eight jobs listed in apply-monitors.sh emitted NO metric at all, so all
four sat in NO DATA from the moment they were created. A monitor that has
never once been green is a monitor somebody mutes, and muting it removes the
only alert on the job that is actually broken. `job-outcome-coverage.test.ts`
now fails if a monitored job has no `reportJobOutcome({ job: "…" })` call.
The tags are load-bearing too, not decoration: apply-monitors.sh finds the
monitor it is about to update by listing `managed-by:apply-monitors` and
matching on name. Without a narrowing tag that listing is every monitor in

_no_data_ceiling_rationale: DATADOG CAPS no_data_timeframe AT 4320 MINUTES (72h). Measured, not read:
35 of 37 monitors were refused 400 "No data timeframe must be <= 4320" on
the first live apply. Everything below follows from that ceiling.
notify_no_data only means something when its timeframe EXCEEDS the job's
legitimate maximum gap. Otherwise it fires on a healthy schedule, gets
muted, and the monitor is worse than absent - which is MONEY-1238.
The WINDOW is already sized to exceed that gap (a week-long cron
window < 4320 min -> no_data = min(3x window, 4320), notify TRUE.
72h still exceeds a sub-72h gap, so clamping is safe.
window >= 4320 min -> the gap is at or past Datadog's ceiling and NO
valid timeframe exists. notify FALSE, deliberately.
